#############################################################
# SNP association analysis with batch correction (snpStats)
#
# Pipeline:
#   1. Load PLINK data, fixing duplicate SNP/sample IDs
#   2. Load phenotype + batch data, align sample IDs
#   3. Run batch-adjusted SNP association tests (snp.rhs.tests)
#   4. Filter for significant SNPs (p < 0.05)
#   5. Check which significant SNPs fall within genes of interest
#############################################################

## ---- 1. Install and load packages ----
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("snpStats")

library(snpStats)
library(dplyr)


## ---- 2. Fix the .bim file ----
# Original SNP IDs (column 2) were all "." which read.plink()
# cannot use as unique row names. Regenerate unique IDs from
# chromosome:position:allele1:allele2.
bim <- read.table("wholegenomevariants_updatedfamvarID.bim",
                   header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

bim$V2 <- paste(bim$V1, bim$V4, bim$V5, bim$V6, sep = ":")

# sanity check -- should be mostly/all FALSE (i.e. unique)
table(duplicated(bim$V2))

write.table(bim, "wholegenomevariants_updatedfamvarID_fixed.bim",
            row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)


## ---- 3. Fix the .fam file ----
# Original FID/IID columns contained periods, which broke
# read.plink()'s internal ID-parsing (sep = "." regex collision).
# Replace periods with underscores.
fam <- read.table("wholegenomevariants_updatedfamvarID.fam",
                   header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

fam$original_id <- fam$V1  # keep original IDs for reference

fam$V1 <- gsub("\\.", "_", fam$V1)
fam$V2 <- gsub("\\.", "_", fam$V2)

write.table(fam[, 1:6], "wholegenomevariants_updatedfamvarID_fixed.fam",
            row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)


## ---- 4. Copy .bed file to match the new fixed base name ----
file.copy("wholegenomevariants_updatedfamvarID.bed",
          "wholegenomevariants_updatedfamvarID_fixed.bed")


## ---- 5. Load the fixed PLINK files ----
data <- read.plink("wholegenomevariants_updatedfamvarID_fixed.bed",
                    na.strings = c("0", "-9"),
                    sep = "_",
                    select.subjects = NULL,
                    select.snps = NULL)

snpmatrix <- data$genotypes

# confirm unique sample IDs
length(unique(rownames(snpmatrix))) == length(rownames(snpmatrix))

# remove any known problem samples here, e.g.:
# snpmatrix <- snpmatrix[rownames(snpmatrix) != "sample_31", , drop = FALSE]


## ---- 6. Load phenotype/batch data ----
pheno <- read.csv("snpstatsphenotypes.csv", row.names = 1,
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# if columns look garbled (crammed into one), the file is
# actually tab-delimited -- use instead:
# pheno <- read.delim("snpstatsphenotypes.csv", row.names = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

pheno$batch <- as.factor(pheno$batch)


## ---- 7. Align phenotype sample IDs to match snpmatrix ----
rownames(pheno) <- gsub("\\.", "_", rownames(pheno))
rownames(pheno) <- sub("_trimmed_sorted_minq20$", "", rownames(pheno))

# remove matching problem samples from pheno too, e.g.:
# pheno <- pheno[rownames(pheno) != "sample_31", , drop = FALSE]

# confirm alignment
sum(rownames(pheno) %in% rownames(snpmatrix))
nrow(pheno)
nrow(snpmatrix)


## ---- 8. Run the batch-adjusted SNP association test ----
# snp.rhs.tests() fits phenotype ~ batch + SNP_i for every SNP,
# testing whether each SNP predicts phenotype after adjusting for batch.
results <- snp.rhs.tests(
  phenotype ~ batch,
  family = "binomial",   # use "Gaussian" if phenotype is continuous
  data = pheno,
  snp.data = snpmatrix
)


## ---- 9. Extract results ----
# results is an S4 "GlmTests" object -- SNP IDs, chi-squared
# values, and other info are stored as slots (accessed with @),
# not as names() on the p-value vector.
snp_ids    <- results@snp.names
pvals      <- p.value(results)
chisq_vals <- results@chisq

signifp <- data.frame(
  snp_id = snp_ids,
  pvalue = pvals,
  chisq  = chisq_vals,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# keep only significant SNPs
signifp <- signifp %>% filter(pvalue < 0.05)

nrow(signifp)
head(signifp)

write.table(signifp, "significantsnps.txt", row.names = FALSE)


## ---- 10. Check which significant SNPs fall within genes of interest ----

# Genes of interest, as chr:start-end
genes <- data.frame(
  gene = c("TLR1A", "TLR1B", "TLR2A", "TLR2B", "TLR3-1", "TLR3-2", "TLR3-3",
           "TLR3-4", "TLR4-1", "TLR4-2", "TLR4-3", "TLR5", "TLR7", "TLR15", "TLR21"),
  region = c("SUPER_4:53881681-53884137", "SUPER_4:53873407-53875357",
             "SUPER_4:32245726-32248107", "SUPER_4:32236631-32238982",
             "SUPER_4:20103611-20103802", "SUPER_4:20100233-20102059",
             "SUPER_4:20099425-20099652", "SUPER_18:8042591-8042695",
             "SUPER_18:8041589-8041755", "SUPER_18:8037993-8040252",
             "SUPER_3:95457095-95459677", "SUPER_1:77572878-77576018",
             "SUPER_3:116327465-116330056", "SUPER_29:1579922-1582852",
             "SUPER_4:20104648-20105088"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

genes$chr   <- sub(":.*", "", genes$region)
genes$start <- as.numeric(sub(".*:(\\d+)-.*", "\\1", genes$region))
genes$end   <- as.numeric(sub(".*-(\\d+)$", "\\1", genes$region))

# parse chr:pos out of each significant SNP's ID
signifp$chr <- sapply(strsplit(signifp$snp_id, ":"), `[`, 1)
signifp$pos <- as.numeric(sapply(strsplit(signifp$snp_id, ":"), `[`, 2))

# flag which gene (if any) each significant SNP falls inside
signifp$in_gene <- sapply(seq_len(nrow(signifp)), function(i) {
  hit <- genes$gene[genes$chr == signifp$chr[i] &
                     signifp$pos[i] >= genes$start &
                     signifp$pos[i] <= genes$end]
  if (length(hit) > 0) paste(hit, collapse = ";") else NA
})

gene_hits <- signifp[!is.na(signifp$in_gene), ]
gene_hits

write.table(gene_hits, "significant_snps_in_genes_of_interest.txt", row.names = FALSE)
